It records the precise C5/SF.2 supplier frontiers; complete means planned, not closed or implemented.

nodes.title: Cycle classes from first Chern classes
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, F a characteristic-zero field, T a one-dimensional F-space, and H a contravariant unital graded-commutative F-algebra functor on smooth projective k-schemes. Write H^q(X)(m)=H^q(X)⊗T^m, using the dual line for negative m. Assume finite-disjoint-union compatibility; a natural group homomorphism c1_H:Pic(X)→H^2(X)(1); the projective bundle formula in every degree; and the divisor-support condition below. There is a unique natural graded Q-algebra map cl_H:CH^*(X)_Q→⊕_r H^{2r}(X)(r) such that ch_H=cl_H∘ch_CH. In particular cl_H(c1_CH(L))=c1_H(L). Any unital multiplicative cohomology comparison respecting T and c1 respects cl_H in every codimension.
hypotheses: The projectivization is the convention of the SF.5 projective bundle formula, with ξ=c1_H(O_P(E)(1)). For rank s≥1 the map ⊕_{j=0}^{s−1}H^{q−2j}(X)(−j)→H^q(P(E)), (a_j)↦Σ ξ^j∪π^*a_j, is an isomorphism.
For a smooth effective Cartier divisor i:D→X with X,D smooth projective, i^*a=0 implies a∪c1_H(O_X(D))=0.

SF.5 supplies ch_CH:K0(Vect(X))⊗Q≅CH^*(X)_Q, as a ring isomorphism, and its pullback, Adams-weight and Chern-class compatibility. This construction alone does not assert proper-pushforward compatibility or Poincaré duality.
proofSteps: Construct higher cohomological Chern classes by the projective bundle relation; pull back to the flag bundle to verify naturality and the splitting principle. Use the Newton polynomials with factorial denominators to obtain the ring map ch_H with ch_H(L)=exp(c1_H(L)).

Define cl_H=ch_H∘ch_CH^{-1}. The Adams operation ψ² acts by 2^r on the codimension-r Chow part and on the rth cohomological Chern-character part, so the map lands in degree (2r,r). This is the grading argument in 0FIF, rather than an assumption that ch_CH is degree-preserving before its Adams decomposition.

For a multiplicative comparison preserving c1, pull back to the same flag bundle. The projective bundle injection implies that it preserves every cohomological Chern class and ch_H. Compose with the fixed inverse of ch_CH to get compatibility with all rational cycles.
acceptance: The maps are defined on rational equivalence classes, and are Q-linear, unital, graded, multiplicative and natural for the refined pullback on smooth schemes.
Proper pushforward is established separately when constructing each admitted realization; it is not deduced just from this ring map.

nodes.title: Normalized comparison of twisted cohomology theories
nodes.statement: Fix two admitted smooth-projective cohomology systems H and K over the same k, with coefficient fields F_H,F_K of characteristic zero, Tate lines T_H,T_K and traces. Let E be a field with specified embeddings of both coefficient fields. A normalized comparison consists of a line equivalence τ:T_H⊗E≅T_K⊗E and degreewise E-linear equivalences c_X^q:H^q(X)⊗E≅K^q(X)⊗E, natural for pullback, unital and multiplicative for cup products. Define c_X^{q,m}=c_X^q⊗τ^m. Require c_X^{2,1}(c1_H(L))=c1_K(L) for every line bundle and Tr_K∘c_X^{2d,d}=Tr_H for every pure-dimensional X. Trace on a disconnected pure-dimensional X is the sum of component traces. All comparisons with mixed dimensions are taken componentwise. These are actual maps, not dimension equalities.
hypotheses: H and K include the first-Chern/cycle maps of chern-character-cycle-map, Künneth maps, finite-dimensional Poincaré pairings, and proper pushforwards adjoint to pullback.
All tensor products use the specified coefficient embeddings into E. The two coefficient fields are not identified.
The line comparison on negative twists is the inverse dual of τ, so tensor and evaluation maps commute. The graded symmetry is (a,b)↦(−1)^{ij}(b,a) in degrees i,j.
proofSteps: Bundle only the displayed maps and equations. Künneth compatibility follows from the pullback and cup-product equations because the Künneth map is the exterior product of pullbacks.
Use chern-character-cycle-map to derive all-cycle compatibility. Derive proper-pushforward compatibility by Poincaré adjunction in comparison-intertwines-correspondences.
acceptance: A comparison exports the chosen coefficient maps and Tate-line map; erasing either can change its normalization.
Identity, inverse and composition comparisons satisfy the same equations; inverse and composition on τ are forced by the tensor laws.

nodes.title: A normalized comparison intertwines every correspondence
nodes.statement: For a normalized comparison c from H to K over E and a proper morphism f:X→Y between pure-dimensional smooth projective schemes of dimensions d,e, c_Y^{q+2(e−d),m+e−d}∘f_*^H=f_*^K∘c_X^{q,m}. For a∈CH^{d+r}(X×Y)_Q, set A_H(a)(x)=pr_Y,*^H(cl_H(a)∪pr_X^*x):H^q(X)(m)→H^{q+2r}(Y)(m+r). Then c_Y^{q+2r,m+r}∘A_H(a)=A_K(a)∘c_X^{q,m}, including r<0. Consequently comparison commutes with correspondence composition, identities, external products and graph pullbacks.
hypotheses: All coefficient changes and τ powers are those of normalized-cohomology-comparison.
The pushforwards are the Poincaré adjoints with the same normalized trace; both X and Y are proper. For arbitrary smooth projective schemes split into pure-dimensional components first.
proofSteps: Pair the proposed pushforward equality against any complementary-degree class on Y. Move f_* across the pairing in both theories, use pullback/cup/trace compatibility, and conclude by nondegeneracy after scalar extension to E.

Apply the resulting equality to pr_Y and use the all-cycle equation from chern-character-cycle-map plus pullback and cup compatibility. The twist count is (d+r)+m−d=m+r, and the degree count is (2d+2r)+q−2d=q+2r.

Composition and the identity follow from the existing Chow composition/diagonal identities, the projection formula and Künneth; the pull–cup–push proof of the inherited correspondence-functor construction applies componentwise. Apply MC.1’s universal property over the original field, rather than invoking the inherited algebraically-closed-base theorem outside its hypotheses. No new intersection theory is constructed.
acceptance: For a graph of f:Y→X in X×Y the square is the original pullback-naturality square; for its transpose, with the required degree shift, it is the proper-pushforward square.
The equality identifies maps on all degrees, including odd degrees; monoidality uses the Koszul symmetry.

sources.match: Poincaré adjunction characterizes pushforward and the pull–cup–push formula describes the correspondence action. The comparison square is obtained by substituting the normalization equations into those formulas.

nodes.title: Comparison on Chow motives and all Tate twists
nodes.statement: For a normalized cohomology comparison c over E, the associated E-valued realizations of rational Chow motives admit a unique symmetric monoidal natural isomorphism C:R_H⊗E≅R_K⊗E extending c on h(X) and τ on 1(1). With M=(X,p,m), R_H^j(M)=im(A_H(p):H^{j+2m}(X)(m)→H^{j+2m}(X)(m)); C_M^j is the restriction of c_X^{j+2m,m} to this image. For a morphism a∈q Corr^{n−m}(X,Y) p its action is the restriction of A_H(a), and these components form the naturality square. The extension preserves units, tensor products, dual evaluation, traces and cycle morphisms 1(−r)→h(X).
hypotheses: The source is the MC.1 contravariant category with rational Chow coefficients: Corr^r(X,Y)=CH^{dim X+r}(X×Y)_Q componentwise, and Hom((X,p,m),(Y,q,n))=q Corr^{n−m}(X,Y) p.

Finite-dimensional graded vector spaces have the Koszul symmetry and are idempotent complete; for ℓ-adic targets, use the corresponding finite-dimensional continuous representations and then the specified scalar/forgetful functor.
Both realization functors already exist by their construction nodes or the inherited universal-property theorem; an invertible Tate image is essential.
proofSteps: comparison-intertwines-correspondences gives c_X A_H(p)=A_K(p)c_X, so c_X maps im A_H(p) bijectively to im A_K(p). Its inverse restricts as well. At the pinned linear-algebra level use LinearEquiv.ofSubmodules, not a new image or splitting construction.
Extend through the Karoubi envelope with the existing karoubiUniversal machinery. natTrans_eq says a component on a retract is forced by the component on its ambient object.
Use τ^m on all tensor powers and dual powers of the Tate line. Every motive is a retract of h(X)(m), so this also proves uniqueness through Tate localization.

Naturality for qap follows by restricting the correspondence square. Tensor compatibility is checked on h(X), h(Y) using Künneth, then restricted to p⊗q; τ^{m+n}=τ^m⊗τ^n handles twists. The Koszul symmetry gives the symmetric constraint. Dual evaluation and trace are preserved by a symmetric monoidal natural isomorphism.
acceptance: C_{1(m)} is τ^m in degree −2m and zero in all other degrees; C_{h(P¹)} respects 1⊕1(−1).

For p=0 the component is the unique map of zero spaces; for p=id it is exactly the original c_X with its twist. Composition and inverse of comparisons agree with composition and inverse of the induced natural isomorphisms.
Uniqueness includes the fixed restrictions on h(X) and the Tate line; no choice-free assertion is made after forgetting these identifications.

nodes.title: Betti realization for a specified complex embedding
nodes.statement: For a field embedding σ:k→C, construct the Q-linear symmetric monoidal functor R_B,σ from rational Chow motives over k to finite-dimensional Z-graded Q-vector spaces with Koszul symmetry. On h(X), it is H_B^q(X)=H_sing^q(X_σ(C),Q). The Tate line is T_B=Q(1)=(2πi)Q, with the standard i, and R_B^j(X,p,m)=im p on H_B^{j+2m}(X)(m). The cycle map is cl_B:CH^r(X)_Q→H_B^{2r}(X)(r); for an integral cycle it agrees with its complex-oriented topological fundamental class tensored with (2πi)^r. The trace divides out the Tate generator and evaluates on the oriented fundamental class of each connected component, then sums.
hypotheses: X is smooth projective over k; analytification is taken only after σ-base change. Rational Chow correspondences, not all singular cohomology linear maps, are the source morphisms.

Use singular cohomology, cup products, Künneth and manifold Poincaré duality from the existing AlgebraicTopology roadmap. Analytification and analytic cycle integration come from C5. No second singular or smooth de Rham theory is introduced.
proofSteps: Define c1_B(L) as the connecting class for 0→2πi Z→O_an→O_an^×→1, after algebraic line-bundle analytification, then rationalize. Verify the four first-Chern hypotheses using the topological projective bundle formula and the divisor Thom/support relation; request their precise shared-carrier exports from C5 and AlgebraicTopology.

Apply chern-character-cycle-map. Identify this cycle map with the topological fundamental class using the divisor normalization, the splitting/Chern-character construction, and the supplied cycle integration/Gysin agreement. For proper maps, adjunction and the pushforward of oriented fundamental classes give cycle pushforward compatibility.

Künneth, finite-dimensional Poincaré duality and the normalization of a geometric point verify the Weil inputs of the inherited correspondence construction. On non-geometrically connected schemes retain all geometric components; never impose one-dimensional H^0 there.

Apply the MC.1 universal property over k directly to the pull–cup–push functor and its invertible P¹ top summand. This reuses the inherited construction without incorrectly invoking its algebraically-closed-base hypothesis for k.
acceptance: The construction exports actual maps for graph pullback, proper pushforward, products, twists and trace; all are computed in the common formula in comparison-on-chow-motives.
The embedding σ is an argument of the functor. A different embedding is a different Betti realization unless an explicit comparison is supplied.

nodes.title: Algebraic de Rham realization in characteristic zero
nodes.statement: For any characteristic-zero field k, construct the Q-linear symmetric monoidal functor R_dR from rational Chow motives over k to finite-dimensional graded k-vector spaces. On h(X), H_dR^q(X/k)=hypercohomology of the algebraic de Rham complex Ω^•_{X/k}; T_dR=k(1) is a formal one-dimensional line with distinguished basis t_dR, and R_dR^j(X,p,m)=im p on H_dR^{j+2m}(X/k)(m). With the Čech/shift convention of Hodge II §2.2.4.1, c1_dR is the negative of the hypercohomology map induced by dlog:O_X^×[−1]→Ω^•_{X/k}. The cycle map is chern-character-cycle-map. The trace is normalized by a geometric point after base change; over C it is (2πi)^{−d} times integration of the raw de Rham class, after trivializing t_dR^d.
hypotheses: The characteristic-zero assumption is essential. No de Rham Weil realization in characteristic p is asserted.
For arbitrary k use the C5 algebraic de Rham/base-change export requested below; a chosen embedding k→C is not part of R_dR. The formal Tate line is retained even though its underlying k-space is k.

Use the same total-complex/shift signs as Hodge II §2.2.4.1 and §2.2.5.1. With another totalization convention transport the definition through its specified chain isomorphism, keeping c1(O_P¹(1)) of trace +1.
proofSteps: Use C5 for the algebraic de Rham complex, its products and scalar extension. Construct c1_dR by the displayed negative dlog hypercohomology map. Hodge II §2.2.5.1 compares this sign with the exponential-sequence class.

For a finitely generated subfield k0 of characteristic zero, choose an embedding k0→C. C5 comparison and faithful scalar extension transfer the projective bundle, divisor-support, finite-dimensionality, Künneth and perfect-pairing statements from Betti cohomology. Apply chern-character-cycle-map; its comparison clause gives compatibility in every codimension from c1.

Normalize the de Rham trace via the algebraic duality trace with point degree one; over C its integration formula is as stated. Compare proper pushforward by Poincaré adjunction and transfer cycle pushforward compatibility from Betti.

Every finite scheme/morphism/bundle/cohomology diagram used over an arbitrary k descends to a finitely generated characteristic-zero subfield. The requested de Rham base-change isomorphisms and faithful scalar extension descend these equalities. The maps over k are the algebraic maps already defined; embeddings are used to prove identities, not to define them.
Apply the MC.1 universal property with the P¹ top summand.
acceptance: R_dR is defined even when k itself has no embedding into C, subject to the explicit algebraic base-change supplier contract.
The trace on H_dR^0(Spec L)=L for finite separable L/k is the field trace, so it need not be an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Geometric ℓ-adic realization with Galois action
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, ℓ a prime invertible in k, and k̄ an algebraic closure with G_k=Aut(k̄/k). Construct R_ℓ from rational Chow motives over k to finite-dimensional Z-graded continuous Q_ℓ-representations of G_k, with Koszul symmetry. On h(X), its qth group is geometric étale cohomology H_et^q(X_k̄,Q_ℓ), on the SF.2 coefficient carrier identified with the classical derived finite-coefficient tower. T_ℓ=Q_ℓ(1)=(lim μ_{ℓ^n}(k̄))⊗Z_ℓ Q_ℓ with its cyclotomic action. The value on (X,p,m) is im p on H_et^{j+2m}(X_k̄,Q_ℓ(m)); its cycle map is the EDC.3 Gysin cycle class and agrees with chern-character-cycle-map.
hypotheses: All geometric schemes are smooth projective over the perfect algebraically closed field k̄, so the perfect-base hypothesis of the EDC.3 cycle map holds even if k is imperfect.

For the native pinned pro-étale ellAdicSheaf/EllAdicCohomology carrier, use the explicit SF.2 native-sheaf/derived-limit comparison before identifying it with the classical tower. The existing carrier is not itself this theorem or the Q_ℓ module structure.
Retain the continuous G_k action on maps, twists, cycle classes and projector images. Any later Betti comparison applies the explicitly named forgetful functor.
proofSteps: Import finite-coefficient Kummer classes, geometric base change and finite-generation/continuous-action structure from SF.2; EDC.3 supplies rational-equivalence descent and Gysin/product compatibility. Compare its first Chern class and hence all rational cycle classes with chern-character-cycle-map.

Use EDC.2:pairings for rational Poincaré duality and normalized traces, SF.2 for Künneth and vanishing. Under the finite-to-adic conversion retain 0→lim¹ H^{q−1}(K_n)→H^q(Rlim K_n)→lim H^q(K_n)→0 until Mittag–Leffler is verified. Finite finite-level groups provide that condition in this smooth-proper setting; then invert ℓ.

Pullback to X_k̄ takes k-correspondences to G_k-equivariant cohomology maps. Continuous invariant images of projectors are again finite-dimensional continuous representations. Apply the MC.1 universal property in that idempotent-complete target.
For imperfect k the geometric action is obtained through the separable closure and the purely inseparable-invariance identification requested from SF.2, rather than assuming that k̄/k is Galois.
acceptance: The target is geometric cohomology, not the arithmetic groups H^q(X,Q_ℓ), which generally fail the stated finite-dimensional Weil axioms.
The construction makes no comparison of coefficient fields C and Q_ℓ and no ℓ=char(k) assertion.

nodes.title: The de Rham–Betti comparison on motives
nodes.statement: For σ:k→C, there is a named symmetric monoidal natural isomorphism C_dRB,σ:R_dR(−)⊗_{k,σ}C≅R_B,σ(−)⊗Q C. On h(X) its untwisted component I_X^q is the C5 algebraic de Rham/base-change, analytification, holomorphic de Rham and singular comparison composite. Put p=2πi and t_B=p∈Q(1). The line map is t_dR↦p^{−1}t_B. Thus on H^{q}(X)(m), expressed in the formal Tate bases, the component is p^{−m}I_X^q. On (X,e,m) restrict I_X^{j+2m}⊗τ^m to the image of e. This is natural for every Chow correspondence and preserves cup, pushforward, cycle classes, duality and normalized trace.
hypotheses: Use the fixed C5 proper comparison node and multiplicative-period-interface together with the strengthened first-Chern, scalar-extension and trace contract requested from C5.
The source/target directions are dR→Betti. The inverse has the inverse period on the Tate line. No isomorphism of the original k- and Q-vector spaces is asserted.
proofSteps: Obtain I_X^q from C5 after σ-base change; its coefficient map is σ:k→C. Hodge II §2.2.5.1 identifies the negative dlog first Chern class with the exponential class after including the Tate-line factor.

Trace compatibility is the point-normalized C5 trace square: raw top-degree integration scales by p^d, while τ^d contributes p^{−d}. The first-Chern construction then gives all-cycle compatibility, rather than assuming only equality of divisor degrees.
These maps form a normalized-cohomology-comparison. Apply comparison-intertwines-correspondences and comparison-on-chow-motives.

Verify identity and tower coherence of algebraic base change using the specified C5 maps. This gives coherence after base extension and on all projectors and twists; it does not identify different σ without data.
acceptance: For u∈H_B²(P¹,Q) of oriented integral one, I_P¹²(c1_dR O(1))=p u, but C_dRB^{2,1}(c1_dR O(1))=u⊗t_B and both normalized traces are one.
On the motive 1(1), in degree −2, C_dRB(t_dR)=p^{−1}t_B. Using p instead fails the divisor test.
The comparison of a product is its graded tensor product, with the same Koszul convention.

sources.match: This gives the canonical untwisted algebraic-to-analytic de Rham comparison, which C5 owns.
This identifies the first Chern sign and the twist-normalized class/trace.
The line inclusion and trace formula fix the direction of the period factor; the extension to arbitrary projector motives is the packet’s application of the common comparison theorem.

nodes.title: The étale–Betti comparison on motives
nodes.statement: Let σ:k→C and choose an extension σ̄:k̄→C. For every prime ℓ there is a named symmetric monoidal natural isomorphism C_Bℓ,σ̄:R_B,σ(−)⊗Q Q_ℓ≅Forget(R_ℓ(−)). The finite cohomology comparison is a_n:H_et^q(X_C,μ_{ℓ^n}^{⊗m})≅H_sing^q(X_σ(C),Z/ℓ^n(m)), where the exponential coefficient identification sends t_B mod ℓ^n Z(1) to exp(2πi/ℓ^n); a_n uses its inverse. After the compatible derived-limit/native-coefficient passage and inversion of ℓ, the untwisted h(X) component is b^{-1}∘a^{-1}, where b is geometric base change from X_k̄ to X_C. Its Tate-line map sends t_B to the compatible root system ε_n=exp(2πi/ℓ^n). Restrict these components to projector images and apply the required Tate powers. They commute with cycle class, proper pushforward, cup products, trace and every correspondence.
hypotheses: σ implies char(k)=0. No corresponding Betti comparison is asserted in positive characteristic.
SGA 4 XVI 4.1 is used with the structural proper map X_C→Spec C and torsion abelian coefficients; all degrees are required. Cover-level Riemann existence alone is insufficient.
C5 has no existing all-degree Artin-comparison node. Its exact requested contract is recorded as a gap under the existing C5 owner; the proposed C7 in SF.6 is not treated as an existing stage.
The comparison forgets the G_k action on the right. A G_k action on the Betti Q_ℓ-space can be transported through it and depends on σ̄.
proofSteps: Import the finite comparison from the C5 request: SGA 4 XVI 4.1 gives the cohomology map of sites, natural in X and finite coefficients. Its pullback/cup/unit and Kummer connecting squares are included in that supplier contract.

Apply Rlim to the compatible ℓ^n comparisons, compare with the native SF.2 coefficient carrier, and retain the lim¹ exact sequence. Finite torsion cohomology groups give Mittag–Leffler. Finite generation of singular integral cohomology of the compact smooth manifold identifies its completed rationalization with H_B(Q)⊗Q_ℓ; tensoring Q_ℓ kills any integral torsion, which is not discarded before this step.

The root-of-unity coefficient maps yield first-Chern compatibility. Degree-one geometric-point normalization plus the component trace square gives trace compatibility. Apply chern-character-cycle-map for all rational cycles.
Invert the finite/completed comparison and geometric base-change maps in the displayed order. Apply comparison-on-chow-motives to get a natural isomorphism on all motives.
Coefficient reduction, chosen-root identifications and geometric base-change maps supply the tower cocycle; inherit it after retracts and twists.
acceptance: For P¹ the map carries the twisted hyperplane class to the Kummer hyperplane class and their traces to one.
The scalar ring is Q_ℓ on both sides. There is no chosen or claimed field homomorphism C→Q_ℓ.
The comparison is stronger than equality of Betti numbers and retains the embedding, root system and each coefficient/site map.

nodes.title: Exact realization kernels and permitted quotients
nodes.statement: For each admitted realization H, let I_H^r(X)=ker(cl_H:CH^r(X)_Q→H^{2r}(X)(r)), using geometric base change for the étale theory. For degree-r correspondences a:X→Y, A_H(a)=0 in all degrees if and only if cl_H(a)=0. Thus R_H factors faithfully on morphisms through the idempotent-completed H-homological motive category. For an adequate rational cycle relation J containing rational equivalence, R_H factors through its motive quotient if and only if every J-trivial cycle has zero H-class. A normalized comparison after faithful coefficient extension identifies I_H and I_K and gives the induced comparison on their common homological quotient. In particular the Betti, de Rham and each ℓ-adic kernel agree for the specified characteristic-zero complex embedding. Homological triviality implies numerical triviality, while descent of R_H to numerical motives requires the reverse inclusion I_num⊆I_H, hence equality; it is not asserted unconditionally.
hypotheses: Use the rational Chow groups and the same realization on all degrees; no algebraic Künneth-projector decomposition is assumed.

For a general quotient first define the functor on the quotient correspondence category, then extend to its Karoubi/Tate completion. Do not assume that every quotient idempotent lifts to a Chow idempotent.
Faithfulness refers to the homological correspondence Hom groups and their corners, not to essential surjectivity onto graded vector spaces or fullness onto all linear maps.
proofSteps: Künneth and Poincaré duality identify the degree (2dim X+2r,dim X+r) cohomology of X×Y with the sum of the linear-map spaces H^i(X)→H^{i+2r}(Y)(r). Under this identification cl_H(a) is exactly A_H(a). This is the inherited homological-correspondences-embed argument with explicit twists.

If J is killed, the action passes to correspondence classes and then extends via the MC.1 universal property. Conversely use cycles as morphisms 1(−r)→h(X) to show that factorization kills every J-trivial cycle.

Use injectivity of V→V⊗E for field extensions and comparison-cycle compatibility to identify the cycle kernels. Apply the motive comparison before or after the common quotient; their natural isomorphisms agree on geometric generators and Tate, hence everywhere.

A homologically trivial α pairs trivially with every complementary algebraic β since degree(αβ)=Tr(cl α∪cl β)=0. Therefore I_H⊆I_num. Factoring through the coarser numerical quotient needs the other containment; no standard conjecture is silently supplied.
acceptance: A nonzero degree-zero divisor on an elliptic curve can be zero in all these rational cohomologies while remaining nonzero in CH¹_Q; the Chow realization need not be faithful.
A cohomology comparison does not prove numerical=homological equivalence, algebraicity of all Künneth projectors, or independence of arbitrary Weil theories in positive characteristic.
On a curve the homological and numerical kernels on divisors are both the degree-zero classes, giving a concrete quotient check.

sources.locator: §6, pp.7–8, discussion of realization through homological versus numerical equivalence
sources.match: The obstruction to numerical descent is the missing reverse implication from numerical to homological equivalence.
Degree and Poincaré/Künneth pairing identify correspondence kernels; the universal property extends the quotient functor without requiring idempotent lifting.

nodes.title: Degree, first Chern class and trace on a curve
nodes.statement: Let C/k be a smooth geometrically connected projective curve and D a rational divisor class. For each admitted H, cl_H(D)=c1_H,Q(D)∈H²(C)(1), where c1_H,Q is the Q-linear extension of D↦c1_H(O_C(D)) on integral divisors, and Tr_C(cl_H(D))=deg_k(D). Thus this class is zero exactly when deg_k(D)=0. For f:C→C′ a finite morphism of smooth geometrically connected projective curves, Tr_{C′}(f_*cl_H D)=deg D and f_*f^* on cohomology is deg(f) times the identity. Every defined motivic comparison carries these divisor, pushforward and trace maps to the matching maps. Over a complex embedding, raw de Rham integration of the class of D is (2πi)deg D, while the twisted comparison and normalized trace give deg D.
hypotheses: Betti requires σ:k→C, de Rham requires char(k)=0, and étale requires ℓ invertible in k. The assertions are made only for the admitted theories in those domains.

For a rational divisor define c1_H,Q by Q-linear extension from integral divisors; O_C(D) itself is used only when D is integral. Include residue degree and any inseparable multiplicities for a closed point after geometric base change.
proofSteps: Use the first-Chern construction for divisor compatibility. After a geometric field extension, the normalized trace is one on each geometric point with its cycle multiplicity; Chow degree/base-change compatibility gives deg_k(D).

Geometric connectedness makes H²(C)(1) one-dimensional and trace an isomorphism. For de Rham this follows by faithful scalar extension; for Betti and étale it is the proper Poincaré trace theorem. Hence the class vanishes precisely for degree zero.

Use proper cycle pushforward and the projection formula for f, retaining its degree in the Chow push–pull identity. Apply the named correspondence comparisons to the graph and transpose graph to get the commuting squares.
For the complex period calculation apply de-rham-betti-motivic-comparison to D and evaluate the raw top-degree Betti class on the positively oriented curve.
acceptance: For C=P¹ and D a k-rational point, all normalized traces are +1; for D=a−b they are zero.
For a finite map P¹→P¹ of degree n, f^* of a point has degree n and f_*f^* acts by n. A degree-one or transpose-graph convention error fails this test.
This checks the exact cycle quotient and named maps demanded by MC.2, not only dimensions of its realizations.

sources.match: The cycle class of a divisor is first Chern, a point has normalized trace one, and proper pushforward/projection formulas give the finite-map calculation.
The normalized de Rham trace differs from raw integration by the explicit power of 2πi.
